title: AI Voice & TTS News Briefing
summary: ElevenLabs launched Dub & Sync (25-language dubbing with lip sync, alpha, 2-minute clips) and confirmed all default voices retire Dec 31, 2026. Also new: ElevenLabs contact-center integrations and linguist review in Ads Engine, Salesforce's open SOV-Transcribe-1 speech-recognition model, and ElevenLabs voice restoration expanding to music.

articles.title: ElevenLabs launches Dub & Sync: one-step dubbing with lip sync in 25 languages
articles.summary: New ElevenCreative app dubs a video and matches lip movement in a single pass for 25 languages (standard dubbing still covers 90+). Reviewers report it is an alpha capped at 2-minute clips; no pricing published. Why it matters: ElevenLabs' first combined dub-plus-lip-sync product, competing directly with HeyGen; pilot on short clips, and secure on-screen speaker consent and AI disclosure.

articles.title: ElevenLabs default voices retire December 31, 2026
articles.summary: All ElevenLabs default voices (e.g., Roger, Sarah, George, Brian, Daniel) expire Dec 31, 2026; suggested replacements are not exact matches. TechSmith confirmed the notice Oct 14; existing outputs keep working but no new audio can be generated. Why it matters: projects, scripts and third-party tools using these voices will break in January; inventory usage and test replacements per language now for pronunciation and tone consistency.

articles.title: ElevenLabs adds contact-center integrations and linguist review in Ads Engine
articles.summary: Nov 4: ElevenLabs voice agents connect natively to NiCE CXone, Genesys Cloud, Amazon Connect and Five9. Nov 6: Ads Engine adds human review so linguists can check translated copy and dubbed audio. Why it matters: a vendor building linguist review into AI dubbing is a useful model for quality checks on AI output. Secondary source; verify against ElevenLabs' changelog.

articles.title: Salesforce releases SOV-Transcribe-1, an open speech-recognition model
articles.source: No Code MBA AI release tracker
articles.summary: Open-weight multilingual model for recorded audio, with plain-language formatting instructions and custom-term boosting. Why it matters: transcripts are the first step of dubbing; a self-hostable model with term boosting could improve names and specialized vocabulary. Secondary source; benchmark against current vendor.

articles.title: ElevenLabs expands voice restoration to music
articles.summary: People with permanent voice loss get free ElevenMusic access to create songs in their own voice; NYU Langone Health and Wounded Warrior Project join as partners. Why it matters: a minor but clear example of consent-based voice preservation.
